synthesis.paragraph: Today's issue features three papers tagged with "Vehicle Routing Optimization Methods," a topic that averaged 0.82 papers per day over the previous 17 days. Two of today's papers cite the 2016 work "Distributive justice and equity in transportation" by Rafael H. M. Pereira and Tim Schwanen, which was last cited 14 days ago. Additionally, the paper "Who rides and who is left behind: a multilevel analysis of new cycling infrastructure use in three Canadian cities" shares three references with the June 14, 2026, paper "An interpretable machine-learning mode choice model incorporating bicycle route quality." These shared references include "Where do cyclists ride? A route choice model developed with revealed preference GPS data," "A systematic review of the effect of infrastructural interventions to promote cycling: strengthening causal inference from observational data," and "Cycling through the COVID-19 Pandemic to a More Sustainable Transport Future: Evidence from Case Studies of 14 Large Bicycle-Friendly Cities in Europe and North America." Finally, both the University of Toronto and Jimei University appear on two of today's papers.
